decision: routed to figure-it-out, not the Feature playbook
why: ambitious multi-part build, two one-way-door decisions, and a correctness claim that needs a real gate

decision: Next.js 16.4.3 + React 19.3 + Tailwind 4, TypeScript, App Router, src dir
why: CLAUDE.md mandates Next.js App Router with Tailwind for websites

decision: sent the 3.4MB bundled Next 16 docs to a subagent instead of reading them here
why: Next's own AGENTS.md says this version breaks from older training data, but the docs would eat the context window

decision: scope grew mid-turn to rockets, asteroids, N-body gravity, time control and an AI layer
why: user sent three follow-ups before any engine code existed, which is the cheapest moment to absorb them

decision: physics engine will be pure TypeScript, no DOM and no WebGL
why: same code then runs in the browser, in a worker, and in a Node route handler, so the AI tools and the CI gates hit the real engine

decision: AI gets tools that call the engine, and is never the source of a number
why: a narrated figure the engine did not compute is the failure mode that would make an engineer dismiss the whole thing

decision: removed cacheComponents and partialPrefetching from next.config
why: the bundled docs say cacheComponents keeps routes mounted as hidden Activity, which leaks a WebGL context

decision: branded units at the data boundary, bare SI inside the engine
why: NASA sources mix au, km, degrees and days, and a silent factor-of-1000 error still draws a pretty orbit

decision: typecheck script runs next typegen before tsc
why: tsc alone fails on the generated LayoutProps type, which cost one confusing error already

decision: measured the real numeric kernels instead of guessing whether we need Rust or C++
why: the user asked if this should be a lower level language, and that is a timing question, not a preference
result: no rewrite needed, see next rows

decision: limiter is the Kepler solve transcendentals, not the gravity sum
why: RK4 with planet positions recomputed runs 2.74e5 steps/s, with them frozen 5.54e6, a 20x gap, and the gravity sum is 1.2 percent of a step
result: limiter named and mapped to source

decision: decided against a lower level language and against a desktop app
why: the 20x win is algorithmic via interpolated perturber positions, bigger than the 2-5x a WASM port buys, and a URL reaches more people than an installer

decision: Horizons is server-side only, Standish and IAU tables get embedded
why: JPL states you may not embed their APIs in a website, and Horizons sends no CORS header, confirmed by curl

decision: fetched 64 Horizons samples as fixtures before writing the propagator
why: the harness has to exist before the thing it measures, or the tolerance gets chosen to fit the result
result: all returned Ecliptic of J2000.0, script asserts single frame

decision: gate asserts against JPL's own published error bars, not a tolerance we pick
why: a tolerance we choose can be widened until the test passes, which proves nothing

decision: wrote the user's pasted API key to .env.local and verified it with a live Opus 5 call
why: needed to know the key works before building anything on it

decision: measured Mercury's relativistic perihelion advance differentially rather than absolutely
why: RK4 is not symplectic so it precesses on its own, and running both arms identically cancels that

decision: first run of the relativity gate returned NaN and found a real bug
why: perihelion interpolation seeded rPrev at Infinity and the start point is a perihelion, so shift was Infinity over Infinity

decision: demonstration registry is the single list and the gate derives from it
why: a separate list of what to test would go stale the first time someone added a demonstration

decision: stopped quoting a recovered planet mass where the elements cannot resolve it
why: Mars printed 11595 percent, which reads as a broken simulation rather than as a precision limit
result: now quotes Jupiter and Saturn only

decision: restructured the ephemeris gate to RMS plus a declared per-body ceiling
why: JPL publishes nominal errors, not bounds, so asserting every epoch inside them failed a correct implementation
result: 17 ephemeris tests green, no tolerance quietly widened

decision: Neptune is 31 arcsec RMS against a 10 arcsec nominal and that is a real limit, not a bug
why: an independent second implementation reproduced the residuals to three decimals and perturbing eccentricity made both channels worse
result: declared and surfaced, will show in the UI

decision: each body gets one contract and a gate that checks it against its own physics
why: the user asked for a per-planet contract, and a contract nothing verifies is a comment

decision: chose centralized Viewport ownership for the render core
why: two design runners on different models independently picked it and rejected the decentralized shape on the same ground, split ownership of transform writes

decision: eslint zone rule silently did nothing until a planted violation exposed it
why: flat config resolves a rule by last match not union, so the second block disabled the first

decision: Atlas V is the ascent gate vehicle, not Falcon 9
why: ULA publishes stage masses, engine data and a payload against a defined orbit; SpaceX publishes no stage masses and no reference orbit
